heard: A tiny moon is the widest world in the solar system. Enceladus reflects nearly 100% of the sunlight, hitting its frozen shell. Astronomer William Herschel first spotted this 500-kilometer ice ball back in 1789. Its extreme brightness comes from a gravitational tug-of-war with Saturn and the moon Dione. This tidal flexing generates enough internal heat to melt a global ocean beneath the ice. In 2005, the Cassini spacecraft discovered massive geysers erupting from fractures called tiger stripes. These plumes spray ice and organic molecules directly into space to build Saturn's E-ring. Most of that material eventually falls back as fresh snow. That is why a tiny moon is the widest world in the solar system.
